name: Lengthening over nail (LON)

lead: Lengthening over nail (LON) is a surgical route to added height: the leg bone is gradually lengthened, and a rod placed inside the bone carries the load so the external frame comes off earlier than in conventional frame-only lengthening.

The bone is cut and slowly distracted by an external fixator while an intramedullary nail sits in place; once the target length is reached the frame is removed and the nail is locked to hold the bone through consolidation. A randomised study of 31 limbs compared it with conventional Ilizarov lengthening, a 2012 study compared it with internal kinetic distraction and reported fewer complications with LON, and a 2020 systematic review covered outcomes of cosmetic stature lengthening.

paras: People who pursue it treat it as a major, planned surgery with a long recovery: a stretch of gradual lengthening, a period with the frame on, then consolidation and physiotherapy before returning fully to normal activity. It is discussed alongside fully internal motorised nails as one of the cosmetic height options, and the shorter frame time is the main reason people choose it.

Reported complications include pin-site infection, delayed bone healing, and demanding rehabilitation. One study found that reamed nailing can adversely affect bone regeneration during distraction. It is a major elective surgery, and regulation of cosmetic lengthening varies by country.

chain: Bone lengthened with nail and fixator
Added height, faster return to normal life
angle.text: LON adds measurable centimetres of height by lengthening the leg bone with an external frame while a nail inside the bone does the load-bearing, so the frame comes off sooner. It has been reported in both cosmetic and non-cosmetic surgical series.

lead: Lengthening over nail (LON) is a limb-lengthening technique in which an intramedullary nail is placed in the bone and an external fixator is used for distraction, after which the fixator is removed while the nail remains [1][2]. It was developed to minimise the time patients wear a frame during femur lengthening [1].

A prospective randomised study of 31 limbs compared LON with conventional Ilizarov lengthening on length gain, external fixation index, consolidation index and complications [2]. A 2012 study compared LON with intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction in femoral lengthening and reported fewer complications with LON [1]. A 2020 systematic review addressed outcomes and complications of cosmetic stature lengthening [3], and series have reported results of cosmetic lower limb LON [4][5].
infobox: Reported in case series and a systematic review

paras: LON was developed to reduce or eliminate frame time during femur lengthening compared with conventional ring-fixator lengthening [1]. Magnetic internal lengthening nails are a related approach that avoids external devices [6]. Reference sources on distraction osteogenesis describe motorised internal nails as an alternative to external devices [7].

In a prospective randomised study of 31 limbs in 28 patients, 15 were lengthened over a nail and 16 conventionally, and the groups were compared on fixation index, consolidation index and complications [2]. A study comparing LON with intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction found fewer complications with LON [1]. Bilateral tibial LON has been reported with complications and psychological outcomes in a Vietnamese series [5], and results of cosmetic lower limb LON have been published [4]. A study of tibial lengthening found that reamed intramedullary nailing had an adverse effect on bone regeneration during distraction [8]. A 2020 systematic review covers cosmetic stature lengthening outcomes and complications [3]. Related studies include biological enhancement of bone healing in tibial distraction with bone marrow concentrate and platelet-rich plasma [9].

Registered studies include LON pain beliefs and functional performance after cosmetic lengthening (not yet recruiting) [10], postoperative physiotherapy after cosmetic femoral lengthening [11] and video-feedback rehabilitation after bilateral femoral lengthening [12].

Reference sources note that cosmetic stature lengthening is unregulated in some countries, that infection, additional surgeries and shorter-than-expected gains have been reported, and that China's health ministry banned limb lengthening in 2006 after serious side effects [7].

timeline.event: Study reports fewer complications with LON than intramedullary skeletal kinetic distraction [1].
Randomised comparison of LON and conventional Ilizarov lengthening published [2].
Systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening published [3].
